extracted.intended_audience: ACUS staff, consultants, committee members, policymakers, and members of the public interested in ACUS recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the formal ACUS process for producing Recommendations and Statements: commissioning studies, preparing comprehensive research reports with proposed recommendations, committee drafting, Council and Assembly approval, and implementation. Also distinguishes Statements from formal Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory function: convene public and private sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACUS's work should involve both public and private sector perspectives, aiming to identify and recommend process improvements to administrative/regulatory systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement of consultants or in‑house staff
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of the Council, engages consultants to study administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies may be performed by external consultants or in‑house staff; Council approval is required before engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive research report proposing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants or in‑house staff then prepare a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The product supporting a Recommendation is a comprehensive research report that presents proposed recommendations grounded in the study; substantive research is expected to underpin recommended changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discussion and draft Recommendation preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACUS committee discusses this report, preparing a draft Recommendation to submit to the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A committee review and deliberation stage is required, during which a draft Recommendation is developed from the research report for Council consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council approval and Assembly adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: With approval [by the Council], to the Assembly. Following a debate the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal approval process: the Council must approve submission of the draft to the Assembly; the Assembly debates and then adopts the final Recommendation—these approval steps are required for formal adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation commitment for adopted Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption carries an institutional commitment by ACUS to undertake implementation actions for the Recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Statements as alternative outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the ACUS membership has acted to adopt a 'Statement' to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements are typically produced by the same process that leads to Recommendations but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments rather than formal recommendations. (ACUS has adopted 19 such statements, which are included in the searchable database of recommendations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in searchable database
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations and adopted Statements are included in the searchable database of recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted outputs (Recommendations and Statements) are cataloged and made publicly searchable as part of ACUS's records.
